user_goal: Forschungsrun 1; remove the highest-value J-Space/Qwen3-0.6B scientific blocker possible within current authority.

current_main_scientific_lineage.observed_basis: AFFIRMATIVE - 0.5*(NEGATIVE+NEUTRAL), derived from internal activation families
current_main_scientific_lineage.observed_output_counterbalance: AFFIRMATIVE maps once each to A/B/C per calibration and holdout split
current_main_scientific_lineage.observed_remaining_limit: all current calibration and holdout cases request AFFIRMATIVE

new_material_finding.finding_1: The derivation prompts explicitly contain AFFIRMATIVE, NEGATIVE or NEUTRAL in every semantic family, and evaluation templates reuse those semantic class words. Therefore the activation contrast is not lexical-family independent.
new_material_finding.finding_2: Official Qwen3-0.6B configuration reports hidden_size=1024, num_hidden_layers=28 and tie_word_embeddings=true. With tied input/output embeddings, uses_output_head_weights=false is necessary but does not by itself exclude an embedding/unembedding-adjacent lexical shortcut caused by repeated class-token identity.
new_material_finding.finding_3: The current one-dimensional vector contrasts AFFIRMATIVE with the centroid of NEGATIVE+NEUTRAL. Its sign flip therefore points toward the combined non-affirmative centroid, not uniquely toward NEGATIVE. A three-class semantic inversion claim is underdetermined on this axis.
new_material_finding.finding_4: The existing 3-case calibration and 3-case fresh holdout are exactly disjoint by seed/family but remain template-narrow; they are insufficient to discriminate robust semantic transfer from family-local behavior if promotion is intended to mean a general semantic causal direction.

counterhypotheses.statement: The cvec increases requested-code compliance/confidence/task engagement rather than AFFIRMATIVE-specific semantics.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: balance requested semantic targets; require treatment-by-semantic-target interaction rather than aggregate correct-code uplift

counterhypotheses.statement: The derived direction is substantially driven by lexical identity of class words or their embedding/unembedding-adjacent representation rather than a transferable semantic relation.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: derive from matched counterfactual prompts with no class-label or output-code tokens and require vocabulary/template-disjoint holdout transfer

counterhypotheses.statement: SIGN_FLIP is only movement toward a NEGATIVE+NEUTRAL centroid and therefore cannot be interpreted as a specific semantic inverse.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: first test a binary AFFIRMATIVE<->NEGATIVE axis with NEUTRAL as off-axis control; only later promote a two-dimensional three-class plane

counterhypotheses.statement: The effect is specific to the tiny prompt/template family and does not transfer as a semantic relation.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: multi-domain lexical-disjoint holdout families precommitted before runtime

compute per-pair activation differences then aggregate and normalize
bind exact prompt, tokenization, activation and vector receipts
evaluation: equal positive and negative requested semantic targets

recommended_successor_discriminator.positive_prediction: +VECTOR increases the positive-target margin while SIGN_FLIP increases the negative-target margin on vocabulary-disjoint holdout; nuisance controls do not reproduce the interaction
recommended_successor_discriminator.generic_compliance_prediction: +VECTOR raises requested-code margins similarly for both target semantics or fails to show the declared interaction
recommended_successor_discriminator.lexical_shortcut_prediction: effect collapses under vocabulary/template-disjoint holdout or is reproduced by label-token/unembedding-adjacent control
recommended_successor_discriminator.diagnostic_only: measure vector projection/cosine against derivation-lexeme and output-code input/output embedding rows; do not treat Euclidean projection alone as causal proof
recommended_successor_discriminator.optional_sensitivity: orthogonalize the candidate vector against a preregistered class-lexeme embedding/unembedding subspace and test whether causal effect survives
